original_interface_changes.before_clause:
Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two bottom endpoints, and its
$D_\infty$ smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints. These
are respectively the $A$- and $B$-smoothings in the stated chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let

In $T$ put $\rho=a^{-1}$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural

original_interface_changes.before_clause:
Fix $n\ge0$ and a rectangle with $n$ distinct ordered endpoints on its top edge and $n$ on its bottom edge. An ordinary $(n,n)$ tangle diagram is a finite generic planar projection in the rectangle of arcs joining these endpoints and finitely many closed curves, with an over/under marking at each transverse double point and no other singularities. Two diagrams are regularly isotopic when related by planar isotopy fixing the boundary and Reidemeister moves II and III. Their regular-isotopy classes form a monoid under vertical stacking, with the $n$ straight strands as its identity. In the fixed crossing chart, $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ by switching the marked crossing, $D_0$ is the cup-cap top/bottom smoothing, and $D_\infty$ is the through left/right smoothing. A positive curl is a type-I kink with determinant crossing sign $+1$; a negative curl has sign $-1$. Define $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ to be the $T$-algebra obtained from the monoid algebra of these classes by imposing, in every interior disk, the Dubrovnik relations
$$D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty),\qquad \text{positive curl}=a\,\text{straight strand},\qquad \text{negative curl}=a^{-1}\,\text{straight strand},$$
and the free-circle relation that adjoining one disjoint circle with no crossings with the tangle multiplies it by $d$. The symbols $a,z_D,d$ are the images from the coefficient extension. No type-I move is imposed as a regular isotopy; its effect is represented by the displayed curl relations.

original_interface_changes.before_clause: Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is cup-cap top/bottom and $D_\infty$ is through left/right. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

original_interface_changes.before_clause: For each integer $n\ge0$, let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}+z)$, with $z_D=-q+q^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra formed from regular-isotopy classes with crossing rule $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, and free-circle factor $d$, where $D_0$ is cup-cap and $D_\infty$ is through. Number its $2n$ boundary endpoints in cyclic order as $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. A connector is a perfect matching of these endpoints. Orient each open strand from its lower-numbered endpoint to its higher-numbered endpoint and order the open strands by their initial endpoints. Place the finitely many closed strands after the open strands in any fixed order, with a chosen orientation and initial point for each. A diagram is totally descending if, in this traversal order, the first branch encountered at each crossing is the overpassing branch. Then $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ is spanned by one loop-free, self-crossing-free totally descending tangle for each connector. These representatives can have crossings between distinct strands; their crossing data are fixed by the total traversal order. For $n=0$ the single representative is the empty tangle, and for $n=1$ it is the straight strand.

original_interface_changes.before_clause:
Use the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho^{-1}$ and $d=\delta$. On input an integer $n\ge1$ and a finite signed Artin braid word
$$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m},\qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\},\quad 1\le i_j<n,$$
perform the following finite computation:

1. Form the BMW product $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$.
2. Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_m}$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, counting fixed points.
3. List the perfect matchings of the $2n$ tangle boundary endpoints and their standard descending representatives $T_m$. For each signed generator, form its finite left-multiplication matrix in this basis: its column at $T_m$ is obtained by reducing the tangle $g_i^{\pm1}T_m$ to the unique matching coordinates. In each reduction, use the standard endpoint traversal order, choose the first crossing whose first traversal branch is under, and for its current sign $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ replace
$$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
The switched branch has one fewer non-descending crossing, and each smoothing has one fewer crossing; a descending leaf is reduced by the curl and free-circle rules to its standard matching representative. Starting with the coordinate vector of the identity tangle, apply the generator matrices from the rightmost braid letter to the leftmost to obtain the coordinate vector $v_\beta$ of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$.
4. Form the trace row $t_m=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_m})$ by closing each basis tangle and evaluating its scalar Dubrovnik value, and return
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

Here $\tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta$. The output is the declared Kauffman ambient-isotopy value at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$ in the Dubrovnik parameter convention. All matrices are finite and all coefficients lie in $T$; no division by the skein variable is used.
